mbm-0143.clue: I mailed a whole mystery with one stamp.
mbm-0143.quote: I challenged myself to tell a whole detective story on one postcard. There was no room for the butler, so the umbrella had to confess. It had been dripping on the evidence all along.

mbm-0144.clue: Ask me why the lamp has knees.
mbm-0144.quote: At the market I found a desk lamp with wooden bird legs. The seller sneaked a painted egg into the bag. When I switched the light on at home I finally got the joke.

mbm-0145.clue: The sundial is a juice bottle.
mbm-0145.quote: I set my drink beside the towel and follow its shadow across the stripes. When the shadow reaches the blue one I go home. Unless a friend brings another bottle.

mbm-0146.clue: We never cut into the signatures.
mbm-0146.quote: My classmates signed the lining of my graduation coat. Years later I used the lining to back a quilt. On a cold night I can still find the kid who signed upside down.

mbm-0147.quote: The fair contest was peeling an apple in one long strip before eating it. I beat my best peel by a thumb. My rival curled hers into a rose and won the photograph.

mbm-0148.clue: We get one extra life for washing dishes.
mbm-0148.quote: At our house the winner hands over the controller and dries a plate. The day my sister cracked the last level, we ran out of dishes and started polishing the teaspoons.

mbm-0149.clue: My goggles turn the mountain into breakfast.
mbm-0149.quote: My sister said the snow in her goggles looked like grape jelly. Mine looked more like apricot jam. At the lookout we found a viewer with one lens of each color. Breakfast all the way to the horizon.

mbm-0150.clue: I keep a tin of pencil stubs by the dial.
mbm-0150.quote: My friend and I sketch the sky we can see from our radios. She described her sunset while I drew at dawn. I colored one half of the page orange from each end.

mbm-0151.clue: The smallest boat has a pocket sail.
mbm-0151.quote: I pieced a harbor quilt for my uncle. One sail opens so he can tuck his ferry pass inside. These days he spends longer looking for the right boat than crossing the harbor.

mbm-0152.clue: Does your coin purse smell of cedar?
mbm-0152.quote: I bought a little box at the charity sale, thinking it would hold bus fare. Under the lid was a hand-carved skyline. Now I keep the box empty so you can see the whole town.

mbm-0153.clue: We bring a torch for the walk home.
mbm-0153.quote: The projector quit in the middle of a jungle movie. On the way home my friend shone our torch into the hedge and made a much scarier jungle. We walked pretty quickly after that.

mbm-0154.quote: I used a square of flannel for every rainy Saturday and cotton for every dry one. My summer quilt came out almost entirely flannel. You can feel what kind of year we had.

mbm-0155.quote: There’s a wooden whale at the mini-golf place that spits the ball back out. I sank my first shot through its mouth and bowed to the whale. It coughed the ball right onto my shoe.

mbm-0156.clue: I bring tracing paper to club night.
mbm-0156.quote: We paused our favorite cartoon just before the train left. Everyone drew one cloud from the station scene, then we hung the drawings end to end. Our sky ran the length of the windows.

mbm-0157.clue: We tested the buttons with a polka.
mbm-0157.quote: I sewed a waistcoat for my accordion-playing friend. The buttons kept catching in the bellows, so I hid them under a flap. We tested every last one with a polka.

mbm-0158.clue: I can tell you exactly what a cloud weighs.
mbm-0158.quote: The floating castle in my card game fell over whenever I stood it up. I made it a cloud stand stuffed with two dried peas. Three peas made the cloud wobble.

mbm-0159.clue: Nobody talks when the dog changes channels.
mbm-0159.quote: Our dog learned to step on the remote during ad breaks. Once he found a nature show full of ducks and sat on the button. We watched the ducks in our pajamas until bedtime.

mbm-0160.clue: The sea gets the final serve.
mbm-0160.quote: At low tide we build a sand shelf for the volleyball. After the last point we leave it there until a wave floats the ball back. It never calls the score correctly.

mbm-0161.clue: I can send a whole tune with one finger.
mbm-0161.quote: I learned Morse practicing along to the kitchen clock. My radio friend sent me two bars of my birthday song in dots and dashes. I recognized it before I’d even found a pencil.

mbm-0162.clue: We make the mountain higher every winter.
mbm-0162.quote: We glue one more layer of cardboard to the hill in our homemade game after each New Year’s match. This year the red piece rolled off the summit and straight into somebody’s cocoa.

mbm-0163.clue: The recipe is on page forty.
mbm-0163.quote: I used a shopping list as a bookmark in a cookbook. Years later I found I had everything on the list except one lemon. I finished the chapter walking back from the grocer.

mbm-0164.clue: The visitor signed with a footprint.
mbm-0164.quote: I laid out my radio log to dry after a storm. Our cat walked across the empty line beside a station I’d just heard. It’s still my only call confirmed with a paw.

mbm-0165.clue: Leave some space at the kitchen table.
mbm-0165.quote: I learned the fast part of a choro tune by tapping it on an upturned coffee tin. At my first circle my uncle set the tin beside my chair. I didn’t need it, but I liked seeing it there.

mbm-0166.clue: One dancing shoe has a secret dot.
mbm-0166.quote: I put a little silver dot inside my cousin’s left shoe. At her first folk dance she forgot which foot to start with, so I winked and tapped that toe. She led me all the way round the circle.

mbm-0167.clue: That crown is made of curtain rings.
mbm-0167.quote: I went on as the prince with a crown our costume lady made during the interval. She threaded brass curtain rings onto a headband. I gave such a careful bow that not one ring rattled.
